name: Lynx, Giant
body:
GIANT LYNX
CR 3

This long-haired cat has tufts of black hair growing form the tips of its ears.

XP 800
N Medium animal
Init +4; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 14, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 32 (5d8+10)
Fort +6, Ref +8, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 10 ft.
Melee bite +5 (1d6+2), 2 claws +6 (1d4+1)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks pounce

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 18, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 12
Base Atk +3; CMB +7; CMD 21 (25 vs. trip)
Feats Skill Focus (Acrobatics), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (claw)
Skills Acrobatics +11 (+15 for jumping), Climb +14, Perception +10, Stealth +12, Survival +6, Swim +10; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth
SQ danger sense, uncanny dodge

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Danger Sense (Ex)

A giant lynx has a +2 insight bonus to AC and on saving throws against traps and during a surprise round.

Knockdown (Ex)

When a giant lynx makes a charge attack against a Medium or smaller creature (including if it jumps at least 10 feet toward its target), its claw attacks gain the trip special ability and its bite attack deals an extra 1d6 damage on a hit if the target is knocked prone.

Snow Paws (Ex)

A giant lynx does not treat snow or ice as difficult terrain and ignores increased DC due to slippery surfaces due to snow and ice. The DC to follow a giant lynx’s tracks is increased by 5, or by 10 in snowy conditions.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold forests
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

The lynx is a great cat that makes its home in cold regions, most often in rocky areas above the tree line. They are solitary creatures and are excellent climbers, with thick, gray fur that is spotted, striped, or plain. During the winter months through the summer months, its coat varies from spotted to plain. Its short tail is ringed and tipped with black fur. Its pointed ears are tipped with tufts of long black hairs and its eyes range from green to gray to brown. Its paws are large and covered with thick fur. This helps the lynx distribute its weight when moving across snowy terrain, and they are wary of ambushes and very difficult to track. The average lynx is 2 1/2 feet to 4 feet long and weighs 20–40 pounds.

The lynx is territorial and a solitary hunter, mostly during daylight though lynx are nocturnal. Its diet generally consists of small animals such as rodents, birds, fish, and rabbits. During the winter months its diet includes larger prey such as elk or deer. Prey that is killed is partially eaten and the remaining carcass is buried in thick underbrush or snow. The lynx returns over a period of 1d6 days to finish its meal. Lynxes stalk their prey and prefer to strike from ambush. They primarily use their bite attack in combat, only relying on their claws if they must. A lynx goes for the “kill shot” at first opportunity against its quarry, attempting to sink its teeth into its opponent’s throat.

While usually solitary, some dens may contain a male, female, and 1d6 cubs. Cubs are generally ineffective and nonthreatening in combat. Cubs are sometimes captured and sold on the market where they can be trained and raised.
